notes:
Quick bullets from meetings and internal:
- Company: developer tools startup building an IDE co-pilot plugin for enterprise customers. Goal: best-in-class, low-latency streaming completions inside VSCode and JetBrains.
- Key ask: TTFT (time-to-first-token) guarantees + stable streaming (low jitter) under variable workspace load. UX requirement: TTFT target <= 120ms median, P95 < 220ms. Jitter budget: <30ms at 95th for token inter-arrival.
- Token budget model: per-session budget ~512 tokens with dynamic refill on user typing; want server-side enforcement + client backpressure (so the plugin stops requesting more tokens when budget exhausted). Also want graceful truncation and explicit continuation tokens rather than abrupt cutoffs.
- Backpressure / flow-control: prefer HTTP/2 or websocket streaming with per-connection flow control hooks; need a client-visible signal for 'throttle' vs 'end-of-response'.
- Model/version pinning: Must be able to pin stable code model for a customer (e.g., code-optimized-13B) for consistency across builds. Also want opt-in auto-upgrade channels (canary -> stable) and rollback hooks.
- Cost sensitivity: willing to pay for dedicated capacity for predictable latency but want tooling to tune batching + quantization to reduce token cost for non-critical suggestions.
- Security: VPC option + KMS for secret management. Audit logs for every prompt+response required (redaction policies discussed). Data residency: US + EU regions required.
- Quote from CTO on call: "First token feel is everything — we need the cursor to respond like a native editor, not a second-class network call."
technical_summary: POC scope: 2-week dedicated pool run. Success metrics: TTFT median <= 120ms, TTFT P95 <= 220ms, jitter (token inter-arrival) 95th <= 30ms, sustained throughput 250 concurrent users with <10% degraded responses. Implementation notes: enable continuous batching with small max-batch windows (6-12ms), client-side token budget enforcement, KV/prefix caching for file context, pinned model versions per-customer, and streaming protocol with explicit backpressure signals.
perf_snapshot: local staging (non-dedicated) - median TTFT: 58ms, P95 TTFT: 180ms (note: noisy environment, not production)
early streaming throughput: ~18 tokens/s per connection average; peaks of 45 tokens/s during code completion bursts
observed jitter: token inter-arrival stdev ~22ms, 95th ~70ms on noisy staging — target is to reduce to <30ms 95th on dedicated pool
memory/kv cache: warm cache hit improved average response length by ~12% and reduced token cost per completion
